domain: Enterprise resource planning (ERP) — sales, procurement, inventory, manufacturing, quality, and finance operations (SAP-based)
summary:
This application is a full-scale ERP system covering the core operational and financial processes of a manufacturing/distribution enterprise: taking and fulfilling sales orders, procuring materials from suppliers, tracking inventory and warehouse tasks across plants, running production and quality inspections, and posting the resulting financial transactions. It serves order management and customer service teams, procurement/purchasing staff, warehouse and logistics personnel, quality inspectors, finance/accounting teams, and business/operations managers who need a real-time view of the business through a control-tower dashboard.

The system is organized around classic end-to-end business chains: order-to-cash (create an order, check credit and stock, reserve inventory, release for fulfillment, ship and invoice the customer, post revenue) and procure-to-pay (create and approve a purchase order, receive goods, inspect supplier quality lots and findings). Supporting these chains are master data (companies, plants, business partners, materials, suppliers, cost centers, exchange rates), pricing conditions, production orders and bills of material, and quality lots/findings. A control-tower layer built on dedicated services and views gives managers visibility into open orders, stock, incidents, and objectives, with monitoring-event ingestion, incident acknowledgement, and scheduled reconciliation jobs keeping records consistent.

Integration flows connect these processes across systems: releasing an order runs authorization and credit checks before recording the release and emitting an integration event; supplier quality inspection results can block or release stock; and operational monitoring events feed incidents into the control tower for acknowledgement. Together the pieces give the business a single, auditable operational backbone from customer order through fulfillment, quality assurance, and financial close.

useCases.title: Create a sales order
useCases.description: An order management user captures a new customer sales order for fulfillment.
steps: Order manager submits order details
Order is validated and created via CREATE_ORDER
Order record is stored in SalesOrders/SalesOrderItems for downstream processing

useCases.title: Cancel a sales order
useCases.description: An order manager cancels an existing sales order before or during processing.
steps: Order manager selects the order to cancel
System validates order state
Order status is updated to cancelled via CANCEL_ORDER

useCases.title: Check the status of an order
useCases.description: A user looks up the current fulfillment/billing status of a sales order.
steps: User queries an order by ID
GET_ORDER_STATUS retrieves current order status
Status is displayed

useCases.title: Release a held sales order for fulfillment
useCases.description: An order manager (or scheduled job) releases an order so it can proceed through delivery and billing, after authorization and credit checks pass.
steps: releaseOrder is triggered for an order
Company/customer is checked against authorization rules (CHECK_COMPANY)
Order is checked against credit exposure (CHECK_ORDER)
RELEASE and RECORD_RELEASE record the release
An integration event is emitted for downstream systems

useCases.title: Check and release customer credit holds on orders
useCases.description: A credit/finance team member reviews orders blocked due to customer credit exposure and records credit decisions.
steps: Order is checked against customer credit limit (CHECK_ORDER)
Credit hold is identified
Credit decision is recorded (CreditDecisions)
Order release proceeds

useCases.title: Reserve inventory for an order
useCases.description: Stock is reserved against a sales order to guarantee fulfillment ahead of shipping.
steps: Order requiring fulfillment is identified
Available stock is checked at the plant
RESERVE creates a Reservation record against Stock

useCases.title: Check stock availability for a material
useCases.description: A user checks whether sufficient stock exists to fulfill an order line before committing.
steps: User requests availability for a material/plant
CHECK_STOCK calculates available quantity
Result is returned to the user

useCases.title: Generate a customer invoice for a sales order
useCases.description: A billing clerk creates an invoice for a fulfilled sales order and posts it to financial accounting.
steps: Order is confirmed as delivered/billable
CREATE_INVOICE generates an invoice with line items and pricing
POST_TO_FI posts the invoice to finance

useCases.title: Post a financial accounting document
useCases.description: An accountant or automated process posts a journal entry resulting from a billing or procurement transaction.
steps: Transaction requiring financial posting is identified
POST_DOCUMENT prepares the journal entry
postJournal writes JournalEntries/JournalLines to the ledger

useCases.title: Record a customer payment against an invoice
useCases.description: An accountant records a payment received against a customer invoice, closing out the receivable.
steps: Invoice awaiting payment is identified
Payment amount and reference are recorded
Payment is linked to the invoice

useCases.title: Create a purchase order for a supplier
useCases.description: A procurement officer creates a purchase order to source materials from a supplier.
steps: Procurement officer selects supplier and materials
CREATE_PO creates the purchase order with line items
Order is stored for approval

useCases.title: Approve a purchase order
useCases.description: A procurement manager reviews and approves a submitted purchase order before it is sent to the supplier.
steps: Manager reviews pending purchase order
APPROVE_PO records the approval decision
Order status is updated to approved

useCases.title: Receive goods against a purchase order
useCases.description: A warehouse operator records receipt of goods delivered by a supplier against an open purchase order.
steps: Delivered goods are matched to a purchase order
Goods receipt is recorded
Stock is updated for the received quantity

useCases.title: Inspect and disposition a supplier-delivered quality lot
useCases.description: A quality inspector reviews an inspection result on a received supplier lot and records findings to decide whether to block or release the batch.
steps: Supplier lot is received and queued for inspection
Inspector records QualityFindings against the QualityLot
If failed, the lot is blocked and purchasing is notified
If passed, stock is released for use

useCases.title: Plan and schedule production orders
useCases.description: A production planner schedules manufacturing runs, consuming bills of material, to replenish stock or fulfill demand.
steps: Demand or stock shortfall is identified
A production order is created against a bill of materials
Plan is recorded for execution

useCases.title: Manage warehouse tasks for picking and put-away
useCases.description: A warehouse operator works through generated warehouse tasks to pick, move, or put away stock in support of orders and receipts.
steps: Warehouse task is generated (e.g. from a reservation or goods receipt)
Operator executes the task
Task completion updates stock/location

useCases.title: Monitor open orders, stock, and incidents via control tower dashboard
useCases.description: An operations manager views a real-time dashboard of open orders, materials, stock levels, and incidents to manage the business.
steps: Manager opens the control tower dashboard
Open orders, materials, and stock levels are displayed via ControlTower.Orders/Materials/Stock
Incidents are surfaced via ControlTower.Incidents
Objectives/KPIs are shown via ControlTower.Objectives

useCases.title: Acknowledge and resolve an operational incident
useCases.description: An operations manager acknowledges an incident flagged by monitoring so it can be tracked and resolved.
steps: Monitoring event is ingested via ingestMonitoringEvent
Event is evaluated and an Incident record is created
Manager acknowledges the incident via acknowledgeIncident

useCases.title: Reconcile orders against fulfillment and financial records
useCases.description: A scheduled reconciliation process compares orders against fulfillment and finance events to detect discrepancies.
steps: A reconciliation run is initiated (ReconciliationRuns)
Order and integration events are compared to fulfillment/financial records
Discrepancies are logged as reconciliation results

useCases.title: Create and maintain master data records
useCases.description: A master data administrator creates and updates core records such as companies, plants, business partners, materials, suppliers, and cost centers used throughout the ERP.
steps: Administrator selects a master data object
Record is created or updated
Record is validated and stored
useCases.evidence: enterprise.Companies, enterprise.Plants, enterprise.BusinessPartners, enterprise.Materials, enterprise.Suppliers, enterprise.CostCenters, enterprise.ExchangeRates (master.cds)

useCases.title: Maintain pricing conditions for orders
useCases.description: A pricing administrator sets up and maintains the pricing conditions applied to sales orders and items.
steps: Pricing condition record is created or updated
Condition is scoped to material/customer/plant
Condition is applied during order pricing

useCases.title: Process a customer return
useCases.description: A customer service representative records a return of previously delivered goods against a sales order.
steps: Customer requests a return for a delivered order
Return record is created against the order/delivery
Return status is tracked to resolution
